title: Kernel of coefficient reduction modulo a finitely generated ideal
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\sigma$ any set of variables, and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal generated by finitely many elements. For the multivariate formal power-series ring $R[[X_s:s\in\sigma]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], let $C:R\to R[[X_s]]$ be the constant-series map. The coefficientwise homomorphism induced by $R\to R/I$ has kernel $I\,R[[X_s]]$, the ideal generated by $C(I)$. No finiteness of $\sigma$ and no properness of $I$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0EYB, coefficient reduction for the extended maximal ideal

proof.text: An element in the kernel has every coefficient in I by coeff_map and Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem. Choose a finite generating set s of I. Ideal.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun writes each coefficient as a sum over s.

Assemble, for each generator, the coefficients of these finite sums into a power series. By coeff_mul_C and map_sum the original series is the finite sum of those series times the corresponding constant generators. Every summand lies in I.map C, so the series does too.

Conversely every constant from I is killed by coefficient reduction using map_C. Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap gives the reverse inclusion and antisymmetry gives equality. Empty s and empty variable sets require no case restriction.

mathlib_searches.query: Coefficient reduction of multivariate power series modulo a finitely generated ideal has kernel generated by constant series from the ideal

lean.statement:
theorem ker_map_quotient_of_fg {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (σ : Type*)
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG) :
    RingHom.ker (map (σ := σ) (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) = I.map C
